newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Wharf says cable TV costs not a problem.
newsitem.headline: Wharf says cable TV costs not a problem.

text.p: Wharf (Holdings) Ltd on Friday said the company was well able to carry the cost of its cable television business, dismissing Standard & Poor's reiteration of its negative rating outlook on Wharf as old news.
"Regardless of how much we've spent...the group as whole is able to carry these new businesses and yet retain a gearing of something like 16 percent," said executive director John Hung.

"The borrowings of Cable flows through right through from the support the corporate, they haven't had to go and borrow any money themselves, so with that sort of gearing I don't think any watcher of the company will actually say that you're overstretching or anything of that nature," he said.
S&P on Thursday affirmed Wharf's "A" rating but added the outlook was negative, repeating its rating of August 1995.
Hung said the important point for the company and its banks was the reaffirmation of the "A", while the reiteration of the negative outlook was simply a continuation of last year's view.

"In fact the next term should be for the better, but for the moment they're (S&P) just holding it because they feel that the cable company's performance has not in their eyes stabilised, which is quite understandable because until you reach break-even point in any new business a credit agency having the sort of fiduciary responsibility they have would look at it this way."
Hung said he was "very, very satisfied" with the recent performance of the group's Wharf Cable unit, saying it was signing up new subscribers at a much higher rate than before.
"Operating cost has stabilised now, the only thing is to get the subscriber number up and given time and patience we'll do it," he said.

Wharf Cable chairman Stephen Ng said on Wednesday subsciptions had grown consistently since 1995 at over 10,000 residential units a month to exceed 260,000, and that the unit was on course to exceed 30,000 subscibers by year-end.
Hung said in January the cable unit needed 400,000 subscribers to break even.
Ng said operating break-even was attainable in 1998, while Hung said on Friday he was aiming for the end of 1997.
